newsitem.title: GERMANY: German DAX ends bourse at record closing high.
newsitem.headline: German DAX ends bourse at record closing high.

text.p: Bulls continued to hold sway on the German share market, as the DAX index surged in bourse trade on Tuesday, fired by overnight gains on Wall Street to end the session at its second record closing high in a row.

The DAX ended up 24.52 points at 3,460.59 points, having earlier hit a record intraday high of 3,474.98 and dealers said that an imminent breach of its next key resistance level at 3,500 was on the cards.

"We will see 3,500 (DAX points), and maybe today," said a Frankfurt dealer, who said he was taken aback by the sheer pace of the market's advance, despite continued solid earnings signals for German firms from the strong dollar.
"If this goes on much longer, we'll be at 4,000," he added.
"There is nothing around to break this momentum," said another dealer. "There is no sign here of a consolidation."
Driving the advance, March DTB DAX futures were up 41 points at 3,468.5 points.

Banking shares were in the spotlight after second tier bank DePfa, a mortgage specialist, issued a statement saying Switzerland UBS had bought up a stake in it in the open market, refuelling long established takeover speculation.
UBS said it had no plans to take over DePfa, but speculative interest pushed the German bank's share up and it closed bourse at a new all-time high of 89 marks, up 9.88 percent.
DePfa has generally escaped the takeover talk that has propelled German banking stocks to record highs in the last six months.
Other bank shares were also trading heavily.
Deutsche Bank AG ended up 1.60 marks at 95 marks, after failing to convincingly maintain a break above the technically crucial 95-mark level, dealers said.

Commerzbank AG closed floor trade 1.40 marks higher at 46.40 marks and Dresdner Bank, which had earlier risen 73 pfennigs to 57.48 marks, fell victim to profit-taking to end the session down 15 pfennigs at 57.65 marks.
Meanwhile sports retail group Adidas ended up 30 pfennigs at 167.30 marks, off earlier highs, after reporting a rise in its 1996 operating profit on the back of record sales of 4.7 billion marks.
